# R5 — Exhaustive 249-to-53 contextual observer quotient

Date: 2026-11-18 Asia/Shanghai. Scientific status: AUTHOR_PROVED / EXACT_FINITE_CHECKED / NOT_REVIEWED.
Frozen science `435e77af0d180eac32bd1f9c4c464bc4010b7551`, exact count table `EXACT_R5_ALL_101_BUDGETS.json` SHA-256 `50e87f0194cfb3780e84b7bbb6f9a2dca4f79bb4901cab06f1a5b59256fb470b`.

## Theorem A: exact contextual equivalence for all error budgets

Let the ordered fixed context be `(18,24,82,34,17,144,208)` and let x range over the other 249 named configurations. The ordered eight-state observation game is `H_x=(18,24,82,34,17,x,144,208)`. There are 101 physical budget actions k=214,...,314, each with exact integer observation center N_h(k) and cost k. Correct real observations satisfy `|y-N_h(k)|<=tau/2`; up to any integer f>=0 observations may be arbitrary unmarked errors.

For every real `25845652773852463277015040000 <= tau < 58182461585441404127941754880`, and every action k, classify x by the inclusion-maximal correct-response support masks on the eight *named slots*. The 249 x have exactly **53 distinct full (tau,k) support signatures**, comprising 32 nonsingleton classes and 21 singletons. Thus **196/249 choices** are redundant in this exact fixed-context scalar game. The two largest classes contain 28 states each. The pair `{0,48}` is an exact example.

Identical support signatures induce identical adversarial Bellman transition graphs (and equal action costs), for every f and every possible vector of candidate-wise error counters. Hence x in the same class gives identical adaptive minimax cost and identical forced-first-query profiles, at every tau of the interval. The equivalence maps x's position, not its native X6 identity or provenance.

## Finite-completeness proof

At real reading y, correct support is `S(y)={i: |y-c_i|<=tau/2}`. Every maximal S(y) is realized by some closed center window `[c_j,c_j+tau]` starting at a center c_j: slide the feasible window left until its first included center is the left endpoint. Enumerate eight windows and discard strict subset masks. Independently, sweep every doubled-observation boundary `2c_i±tau` and adjacent open cell, taking its inclusion-maximal masks. Both exact methods agree.

Supports can change only when tau crosses an integer pairwise center difference `|c_i-c_j|`. Exhaustively enumerate all 101 budgets and all 32,640 named-state pairs in frozen integer table: **17** distinct internal differences produce **18** half-open real chambers. Evaluate each chamber at the inclusive left boundary, correctly retaining closed-interval equality. The exhaustive 249 x 101 k x 18 chambers support signatures partition into 53 classes. All 53 representative classes are independently checked at 101 x 18 positions by event sweeping: **96,354 exact family crosschecks**. The complete class partition and all 17 threshold values are regenerated by `VERIFY_R5_249_CONTEXT_CLASSES.py`; locally executed exit code zero with `PASS_R5_249_CONTEXT_CLASSES_ALL_F`.

## Theorem B: eight-error exact endpoint calculation for a completed prefix

Using the already pinned eight-state C++ exact Bellman solver and independent support generators, the first 19 classes (ascending representative x) were solved at both tau=L and tau=U-1 for f=8. These classes contain 64 candidate x. Every one of the 38 endpoint computations returned **8335**. Since optimal minimax cost is nondecreasing in tau, each of these 64 eight-state cases has cost 8335 across the entire real fifth-noise interval. Representatives: `0,1,2,3,4,5,8,16,19,20,21,32,33,35,36,37,40,64,65`. Full endpoint memo state counts are in `RESULTS_SUMMARY.json` and in the local reproducibility package.

The remaining 34 classes were not all completed at f=8 in this run. Full-256-state f=8 bounds remain `8335 <= C8* <= 8343`; this does not assert a new global lower bound. No new formal CLAIM, Result/Review admission, native X6 quotient or other owner's execution is claimed.

## Reproduction / next

Run `python3 VERIFY_R5_249_CONTEXT_CLASSES.py EXACT_R5_ALL_101_BUDGETS.json` against the frozen exact integer table with SHA-256 given above. It writes all 53 groups, thresholds, and scope to `R5_249_CONTEXT_CLASSES.json`. The pinned table and original exact C++ Bellman solver are included in the companion local artifact archive. Next, solve each of the 34 unfinished class representatives at f=8 using guarded time/memory bounds, then examine nine-plus-state forced-root obstructions for k=216,223,296. The earlier 77-budgets exclusion certificate is retained.
